summary:
Hauts-de-France has no regional statute of its own on detention, identity documents or anti-discrimination; the region stands under France's national framework, and the sources yield no region-specific legal signal beyond one documented custodial case.

Paola, a trans woman recorded as male on her identity documents and on that basis held in an all-male establishment, was transferred in 2014 to the Lille correctional facility. Detainees there shouted "We don't want any women here!", a fellow inmate tried to attack her with a knife, and she spent two days in solitary confinement. The case is the region's clearest evidence of how placement by civil status operates in practice: threat from other prisoners, followed by isolation of the person targeted.

No other enforcement incident, document-friction account, facilities dispute or care-access finding specific to Hauts-de-France appears in the inventory. The national assessment carried by the France record applies to visitors and residents here without regional modification.
tangentialFactors:
The Lille case is a single data point, not a regional rate. The Ministry of Justice counted 13 transgender detainees across eight facilities nationwide as of 1 November 2016, and the BuzzFeed News investigation of 12 January 2018 named only a handful of cases across the country. Neither source gives facility locations or per-region figures, so the frequency of such incidents inside Hauts-de-France cannot be established from them.

Controller-general of penitentiary institutions Adeline Hazan, quoted in that same investigation, identifies trans women held in all-male facilities as the group that "suffers the most" in prison. Paola's transfer to Lille placed her squarely in that category, which is why the incident reads as an instance of a nationally described pattern rather than an isolated local dispute.

The national detention-oversight opinion of 25 May 2021 covers every place of deprivation of liberty, including establishments in this region, but issues no regional breakdown of its referrals or findings.
localsOnly:
No resident-facing rule specific to Hauts-de-France was identified in the sources. Trans residents held in the region's establishments are subject to the placement practice documented at Lille, and the inventory contains no regional data on how often that practice is challenged, upheld or inspected locally.

The sources record no region-specific provision on housing, employment or service access for trans residents of Hauts-de-France, and no regional institution of its own dealing with trans complaints.
outOfScopeNotes:
Kara B.'s detention following her 2016 protest trial took place in Paris and falls outside Hauts-de-France; it is not evidence about this region.

The Ministry of Justice count of 13 transgender detainees across eight facilities as of 1 November 2016 gives no facility locations. Whether any of those eight establishments were in Hauts-de-France is unresolved on these sources.

No regional enforcement statistics, hate-crime figures, inspection reports or border-authority accounts for Hauts-de-France were present in the inventory. The region's exposure to the documented pattern rests on the single Lille case, and the scale of that exposure is not sourced.
